transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sonia Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Narayan (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Carter (CISO, Montclair Health), Marcus Ruiz (Head of Infra), Leah Kim (Compliance), Tom Alvarez (SecOps)
Links referenced: Redwood trust center (https://redwood.com/trust), SOC2 packet (drive link), Controls mapping spreadsheet (link shared in chat)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Emily: Emily here, CISO at Montclair.
[00:11] Marcus: Marcus, infra.
[00:13] Leah: Leah, compliance.
[00:15] Tom: Tom, SecOps.
[00:17] Sonia: Sonia, Redwood SE. Ravi is on as well.

[00:30] Jordan: Cool, main agenda is SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review, review our reports, trust center access, controls mapping. We'll try to cover encryption/KMS approach, RBAC/SSO options, audit logs and data residency. Any additions?
[00:45] Emily: That covers it. We mostly want to confirm controls alignment for our upcoming vendor assessment and check where you store logs and how we can get audit evidence.

[01:05] Sonia: Great. Quick high-level: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and maintains an ISO 27001 alignment program, our trust center has the attestation PDFs and a controls matrix that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks. I'll pull up the mapping link in chat.
[01:20] Tom: When you say trust center, is that self-serve? Do we get read-only access or just the PDFs?
[01:28] Jordan: We typically grant read-only trust center access for named vendor reviewers, and we can export a ZIP of the SOC 2 artifacts if you need. We'll need an NDA for full artifact access, standard stuff.

[01:48] Marcus: For the infra side curious about data residency. Our patient data needs to remain in US regions only. How do you guarantee that for hosted API calls?
[01:58] Sonia: Right, so hosted is region-aware. We can pin requests to a US region, and for Dedicated/Private you can run in your VPC/on-prem. We also have controls for data retention logs and content retention settings are configurable per account.
[02:15] Marcus: Do you have an official data flow diagram we can include in our assessment?
[02:18] Jordan: Yes, we have an infra diagram and a data flow PDF  I'll share after the call. Sonia, remind me to attach.

[02:35] Leah: On encryption: are customer payloads encrypted in transit and at rest? Who holds the keys? KMS?
[02:42] Sonia: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest. We offer customer-managed keys (CMK) through AWS KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments. For hosted customers, we manage keys by default, but can enable BYOK for enterprise arrangements. There was a note about HSM integrations if you need FIPS-level keys.
[03:02] Leah: So for our pedge  sorry, PD, we need customer-owned KMS for PHI, is that available?
[03:08] Sonia: Yes, for Private deployments and for dedicated contracts we can enable customer-managed KMS. For hosted, it requires an enterprise add-on.

[03:25] Tom: Audit logs - what granularity and retention? We need immutable audit trails for admin actions, API calls, model changes.
[03:33] Ravi: We log admin console actions, API request metadata (timestamp, model id, route, request size), and model rollout events. Logs are shipped to our internal logging cluster; for enterprise we can forward logs to customer SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Logstash) and provide long-term retention. Retention length depends on plan but can be extended.
[03:54] Marcus: Is there tamper-evident storage or WORM?
[03:58] Sonia: We can provide S3 WORM for log archiving on request; for most customers we provide signed audit bundles that map to the SOC 2 evidence.

[04:15] Emily: Controls mapping can you walk through how Redwood maps its controls to SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001?
[04:22] Jordan: Sure. The controls matrix maps Redwood policies, procedures and tech controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO clauses. For example, access control maps to RBAC in the console, SSO/SAML for identity, and periodic access reviews are documented in our policy repo. The mapping spreadsheet has references to policy docs and sample evidence names.
[04:42] Leah: Is there a table we can ingest straight into our GRC tool or is it a PDF?
[04:47] Sonia: We have CSV/Excel matrix exports that customers can import into common GRC tools. We'll include that in the packet.

[05:05] Jordan: Quick note on RBAC/SSO: We support SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM for user sync, and fine-grained RBAC with roles and custom permissions. Marcus, am I right that you use Okta?
[05:15] Marcus: Yes Okta. SCIM is preferred.
[05:18] Sonia: Okta + SCIM + SAML is supported. We also have audit logs for SSO events and provisioning actions.

[05:35] Tom: We need to validate your patching and vulnerability program as part of our vendor assessment. Do you publish timelines or have a cadence?
[05:41] Ravi: We run monthly patch cycles for infra and critical patches on accelerated timelines. We have a vulnerability management policy and regular third-party scans; our SOC 2 evidence includes the VM reports summary. We can provide a redacted schedule.

[06:00] Emily: For ISO alignment, do you plan to have an external ISO 27001 cert or is it internal alignment?
[06:06] Jordan: Currently we have ISO 27001 alignment and controls mapping; we are targeting certification next year for full ISO 27001 cert  timeline dependent on audit windows. We do maintain similar control baselines already.

[06:25] Leah: Regarding vendor subprocessing do you list subprocessors and provide notification windows?
[06:30] Sonia: Yes, subprocessors list is in the trust center and we provide 30-day notice for new critical subprocessors. We'll share the latest list.

[06:45] Marcus: On the technical side, can we push logs directly to our SIEM? Or do you only do periodic exports?
[06:50] Ravi: We support real-time streaming to customer endpoints (Kinesis, PubSub equivalents), and log delivery via S3 or syslog integrations. We'll need to configure endpoints and authentication together.

[07:10] Emily: For evidence collection: would Redwood be able to provide example screenshots or console logs showing RBAC, SSO mappings, and audit entries?
[07:18] Jordan: Yes, we can capture redacted screenshots and example audit bundles. For full artifact access we usually ask for an NDA and then create read-only trust center accounts.

[07:35] Tom: A small question  how do you handle model rollouts and verifying that older model artifacts are not accessible after deprecation?
[07:42] Sonia: We have model versioning and access controls. When a model is deprecated we remove the serving endpoints and revoke keys; our rollout logs track who initiated deprecation and the timestamp. That's part of change management evidence.

[07:58] Marcus: Anything to note about caching and KV cache? We need to ensure no customer-specific KV persists across customers.
[08:05] Ravi: Caches are tenant-isolated for Dedicated/Private. For hosted multi-tenant, prefix-based KV cache ensures logical separation; we can provide architecture notes. There are occasional transcribe issues around "KV cash" in some docs, just FYI.

[08:28] Emily: A couple of blocker items for us: 1) we need BYOK/KMS for PHI, 2) read-only trust center access, 3) CSV controls mapping import. If those are deliverable, we can proceed to the vendor approval board.
[08:40] Jordan: All three are deliverable. BYOK is part of dedicated/private contracts; trust center read-only we'll grant once NDA is in place; CSV export exists. We'll put those in next steps.

[09:00] Sonia: Technical deep dive if we schedule a session with Marcus and Tom, we can walk through log streaming, KMS integration guide, and SCIM provisioning flows.
[09:10] Marcus: Good. Prefer next week afternoon.

[09:20] Jordan: I'll send proposed times. Action items as discussed: Jordan share SOC2 artifacts + mapping; Sonia to schedule deep dive; Leah to send residency scope list. Any other open questions?
[09:34] Leah: One last on retention: do you offer customizable retention per tenant for audit logs?
[09:40] Ravi: Yes, retention windows are configurable; we default to 90 days for console logs and 365 days for audit bundles on enterprise plans; can extend with archive to S3 WORM.

[09:55] Tom: For the NDA what's the process?
[09:58] Jordan: I'll share a standard mutual NDA, but if legal wants amendments we can route through our counsel.

[10:08] Emily: Great. We'll wait for the SOC2 packet and then request trust center access.

[10:15] Jordan: Perfect. We'll aim to get the packet out by Wednesday (2026-05-06). Sonia will follow up on scheduling. Thanks all.

[10:27] Jordan: Quick recap of next steps in chat: SOC2 + controls mapping, trust center access after NDA, schedule infra deep-dive, Leah to send residency scope.

[10:40] Emily: Thanks, bye.

[10:42] Everyone: Bye.

End of transcript.
